name: add-food-definition
description: Use when the user names a food to add, asks to add a food entry, or wants a new food written into data-food/definitions-food.json from the Import food nutrition prompt. Writes the Nutrition Facts or restaurant-sheet nutrients into the file first, then fills vitamins and minerals that sheet did not list, including B vitamins, from composition data.
purpose: Add one or more named foods to data-food/definitions-food.json. Nutrition objects follow the Import food definition prompt builder (Have AI help me). When a Nutrition Facts label or restaurant sheet exists, append that sheet's nutrients immediately so the food is in the file, then update the same object with the vitamins and minerals the sheet did not list.
onInvoke: The user named a food (or a list of foods) to add to the sample food definitions. You fill the Import food prompt yourself and append the objects. Do not stop after drafting a prompt for ChatGPT.

When the food has a Nutrition Facts label or a restaurant nutrition sheet, write that sheet into the file before looking up anything it left off. The food has to be in definitions-food.json as soon as the printed nutrients are known.
If they did not name a food, ask which food. Do not invent a food.

If they already named a portion, use that portion. If they did not, follow the serving rules below and write the entry. Ask only when the name is a different food under two reasonable readings (which brand, which recipe), not when only the household serving is unspecified.

files.ui: Import food definition modal → ✨ Have AI help me (#import-ai-panel, #import-ai-portion)

readBeforeWriting: Use rulesFromBuilder in this skill as the working copy. Do not read buildAiPromptFromPortion, jsonSchemaExample, or nutrientListForPrompt unless a key or unit is missing here and is also missing on a recent entry in definitions-food.json.
If this skill and app.js disagree, app.js wins. Open only the field list that holds that key (MICRO_FIELDS, MICRO_EXTENDED_FIELDS, or LONGEVITY_FIELDS).
jsonSchemaExample() zeroes every key as a shape demo. Those zeroes are not data. Do not paste that object into the file.
rulesFromBuilder: Return JSON matching the structure: one object, or an array when there is more than one common serving. Omit a nutrient key only when no composition source reports it.

A Nutrition Facts label is not a complete nutrient list. The FDA only requires vitamin D, calcium, iron, and potassium among vitamins and minerals. Fill the voluntary ones from composition data, including every B vitamin (thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, biotin, folate, vitamin B12) and vitamins A, C, E, and K, magnesium, zinc, selenium, copper, manganese, chromium, iodine, phosphorus, molybdenum, chloride, and choline. Keys and lookup sources are labelGapNutrients and sources in .agents/skills/qa-definitions-food-label-gaps.json. Use the label for nutrients it actually prints. A missing label line is not an omit and not a 0. A label 0% means under 2% DV, not zero. Store 0 only when composition data shows the nutrient is absent (vitamin B12 in an unfortified plant food, vitamin C in unfortified oil). A Supplement Facts panel must list every dietary ingredient, so a nutrient it does not list can be 0. For a heavily fortified product, use the label or the maker's full list for the added premix; do not estimate those added vitamins from the unfortified base food. Enriched bread is a typical miss: the flour adds thiamin, riboflavin, niacin, and folic acid, and the grain supplies other B vitamins, even when the label lists none of them. Cite the composition source and portion weight in notes.
Use the portion in the name field.

If the food is missing serving information, append a common serving size to the end of the food name (e.g. 1/2 cup, 1 cup, 1 oz, 2 oz, 3 oz). Prefer everyday portions people actually log. If the serving is in oz, add a visual reference in parentheses if possible (e.g. "3 oz (palm-sized)", "1 oz (about a small handful)"). If it's usually eaten all in one sitting from a container or bag, name it as container or bag followed by oz etc in parenthesis.

If the food has more than one common serving size people actually log, return an array of objects — one object per serving — with all nutrients scaled to that serving. When the user already named one portion, write only that portion.
Amounts for the micro requirements panel belong in micros. When the same nutrient key also appears in longevity, store the number in micros only and set longevity[key] to true.

If the food is a multivitamin or vitamin entry: Don't just list the label DV. Adjust both the DV and actual values for typical absorption, since we don't absorb 100% of a pill for every vitamin. If there is fat soluble vitamins, assume enough fats were eaten to absorb the fat-soluble vitamins (A, D, E, K).

required.name: Non-empty string. Food, then the serving at the end, matching existing names such as "Lamb steak 3 oz (palm-sized)". Keep the user's wording when it already includes a serving.

optional.micros: object of numeric amounts. Units are whatever nutrientListForPrompt assigns to that key.
optional.longevity: object. Longevity-only keys are numbers. Keys that also exist in micros are boolean true.
optional.carbQuality: object. glycemicIndex (GI, not grams), addedSugar (g), refinedCarbs (g). Also set netCarbs (g) to carbs minus fiber when fiber is known; the file stores it even though CARB_QUALITY_KEYS does not list it.
optional.notes: string. Cite the published source, the gram weight scaled to, and any important omission. When a Nutrition Facts label was used, also cite the composition source for B vitamins and the other nutrients the label did not have to list. The prompt schema omits notes; the sample file includes them.

values: Scale every number to the serving in the name.

Use a published source. USDA FoodData Central or a national food table (CoFID or equivalent) for composition. A Nutrition Facts or restaurant page is a start for branded food: write the numbers it actually prints into the file first, then update that object with B vitamins and the other vitamins and minerals the sheet did not list. Name each source in notes.

A missing Nutrition Facts line is not a reason to omit the key or store 0. A label 0% means under 2% DV, not zero. Omit a key only when composition data also does not report it. A stored 0 means composition data reported zero, or the nutrient is absent for that food (vitamin B12 in an unfortified plant food, vitamin C in unfortified oil). On a Supplement Facts panel, a nutrient the panel does not list can be 0.
Do not copy the zero-filled schema. Do not invent a number with no source. Do fill B vitamins and the other nutrients the label is allowed to skip when a composition source reports them.
Protein, carbs, and fats are required. If you cannot find those three, do not append the food; say what source you checked.
Only use micros, longevity, and carbQuality keys that jsonSchemaExample / nutrientListForPrompt emit, plus carbQuality.netCarbs and notes.
research: Search this file before the web. After the duplicate check, search definitions-food.json for the same ingredient or brand family (another canned fruit, another Trifecta meal, chicken breast, cauliflower, carrot). Reuse its FDC ids and the per-100 g biotin, chromium, molybdenum, iodine, and chloride method already written in that note. Do not open MEXT, NIH, or Anderson for a food type this file already documents.

Lock one label and stop. For a branded food use one USDA branded FDC record or the maker's page. Write down the serving in grams and the printed protein, carbs, fat, fiber, sodium, and any mineral the label gives as a number. A second calorie site that disagrees is not a second label.

Write that label into the file before filling gaps. Append the object with only the printed nutrients, validate the JSON, and only then do the composition steps below. Do not research vitamins and minerals the sheet left off while the food is still absent from the file.

Fill gaps from USDA SR Legacy per 100 g. The foods/search response already includes foodNutrients; save that JSON and do not fetch the same food again. DEMO_KEY returns 429 if you search in a burst: one script, a short pause between calls, and on 429 use the payloads already saved. Do not switch to per-cup HTML (nutritionvalue, MyFoodData, getfoodfacts) and divide by hand.

Compute in code from per 100 g. Copper is USDA mg times 1000. Amino acids are USDA g per 100 g times 10 times the gram weight, which yields mg. Do not transcribe a cup table into an object: two nutrients abbreviated the same way (potassium and vitamin K both as k) overwrite each other.

A prepared meal keeps the label's protein, carbs, fat, sodium, and fiber. Estimate one gram split that sums to the labeled weight and lands near the label protein and fat. Cite each FDC id and gram weight. A few grams off on carbohydrate is acceptable. Do not run an optimizer. Leave garlic, ginger, seeds, vinegar, and stock in the note when they have no separate weight. If saturated, monounsaturated, and polyunsaturated fat must sum to the labeled fat, scale the unsaturated fats once.

If the closest record is missing vitamin E, vitamin K, choline, selenium, or carotenoids, borrow only those keys from the nearest other pack (light syrup when extra light has no value). Do not build a second full blend.

Trace nutrients are last, and only for keys still empty. Prefer a rate already stored on a similar food in this file. Then one MEXT fooddb page or the label-gap sources. Do not parse a MEXT PDF when a per-100 g number is already in a note or on fooddb.mext.go.jp.
Do not run the label-gap QA script, rebuild sources, or commit as part of adding a food. Fill the gap keys on the new object and cite them in notes.
workflow: Search data-food/definitions-food.json for the food name (case-insensitive). Use search; do not load the whole file.
If the same food and the same serving already exist, report the existing name and stop. Do not add a second copy. A different serving of the same food is allowed when it is not already there.
Follow research, in that order. Estimate nutrients with rulesFromBuilder. Open app.js only for a key or unit this skill does not already state.
When the food has a Nutrition Facts label or a restaurant nutrition sheet, add it in two passes on the same object. Do not wait until the composition fill is done to insert the food.

Pass 1, label: append one object per serving with only the nutrients that sheet prints, plus protein, carbs, and fats. Set netCarbs when that sheet prints both carbohydrate and fiber. Notes cite the sheet, the serving, and which vitamins and minerals it did not list. Validate the JSON before any composition lookup. The food is in the file at this point.

Pass 2, gaps: update that same object. Keep every printed number. Fill the nutrients the sheet did not list, including every B vitamin and the other label-gap nutrients, from composition data, and append that source to the notes. Do not leave those nutrients for a later QA pass.
When there is no label or restaurant sheet, build the full object from composition data and append it once.

Append new objects to the end of the JSON array. Put a comma after the previous last object. Match the file's 2-space indent, including the array item itself (the new object starts indented under the array, not at column 0). Do not JSON.parse and rewrite the rest of the file.
Validate after the label pass and again after the gap pass. Then tell the user each new name, its serving, the label source, and the composition source in notes.

duplicateCheck.search: Grep data-food/definitions-food.json for the food words and for "name" lines.
duplicateCheck.sameServing: Stop and report the existing name.
duplicateCheck.differentServing: Append only the new serving, scaled on its own.
duplicateCheck.userNamedPortion: One object for that portion, even if other servings are also common.

also: The file must still be a JSON array.
Each name you just added appears once, and that object has numeric protein, carbs, and fats.
The file already contains a few repeated names. Do not treat those as a reason to reformat the file. Do not add another copy of a name that is already present.

doNot: Do not write the entry only in the chat.
Do not edit definitions-food-categories.json in this skill. If the new name is likely uncategorized, say so. Categorizing is the categorize-food-definitions skill.
Do not change existing food objects.
Do not put a bridge nutrient's number in longevity. The number stays in micros; longevity gets true.
Do not treat a Nutrition Facts label as the full micronutrient list. Do not store 0 for a vitamin or mineral the label left off or printed as 0%.
Do not hold a labeled food out of definitions-food.json until the composition fill is finished. The printed nutrients go in first.
Do not add foods the user did not name.
Do not open a second or third nutrition site after the branded FDC record or the maker's page is in hand.
Do not hand-copy per-cup HTML into per-100 g numbers.
Do not fetch a USDA food again when its nutrients are already in a search response.
Do not run the label-gap QA workflow while adding a food.
